prostate.name: Prostate
prostate.provenance: measured / rule-based on this body's own CT or cryosections (subject ct_vhm_pelvis)

measures.label: Subpubic angle (angle between the axes of the two ischiopubic rami, 3-D)
measures.note: proxy at the symphysis: 79.0 deg. Method differs from the paper's 4-landmark angle (axes of the rami, not their inferior borders): trust the sign, not the last 5 deg.

measures.label: Transverse pelvic outlet (intertuberous distance) / bi-iliac breadth
measures.citation: PMID 24789357, 42793678 (transverse outlet among the most dimorphic)
measures.note: intertuberous 103.5 mm, bi-iliac 280.2 mm; internal reference = the two real donors measured by the same code (VH male, VH female); NOT a population norm (n = 1 + 1): VH male 0.369, VH female 0.403

measures.label: Greater sciatic notch (hull-defect angle at the deepest point, lateral silhouette)
measures.note: depth 43.5 mm. NOT the osteometric notch angle (different landmarks); internal reference = the two real donors measured by the same code (VH male, VH female); NOT a population norm (n = 1 + 1): VH male 80.3, VH female 90.9

measures.label: Ischiopubic index (pubic length / ischial length x 100, from the femoral-head centre)
measures.citation: not found in a PubMed abstract this session (Washburn 1948 is not in PubMed)
measures.note: internal reference = the two real donors measured by the same code (VH male, VH female); NOT a population norm (n = 1 + 1): VH male 114.4, VH female 124.2; the absolute level (>110) is above textbook values because the femoral-head centre stands in for the acetabular centre

measures.label: Sacral index (breadth of the upper half / straight length x 100)
measures.note: internal reference = the two real donors measured by the same code (VH male, VH female); NOT a population norm (n = 1 + 1): VH male 91.0, VH female 105.8. The Z-Anatomy male reads FEMALE-like here (107): the index depends on how the sacral apex / coccyx is cut in each mesh; not reliable across the six pages

measures.label: Sacral curvature index (depth of the anterior concavity / chord x 100)
measures.citation: PMID 34964781 (differs by sex, no direction in the abstract)
measures.note: own male 14 % vs the five other meshes 34-37 %: a mesh / cut artefact (his sacrum is a different decimation), not diagnostic

measures.label: Bi-iliac (maximum pelvic) breadth
measures.note: absolute size is not a sex marker without stature; the ratio to the shoulder breadth is used below

measures.label: Femoral head diameter (sphere fit, right)
measures.note: left 48.1 mm. Absolute values are population / size dependent (31 to 48.5 mm in males across studies); the two real donors read the SAME diameter (VH male 48.7, VH female 47.2 mm: she is 88 kg): not diagnostic here

measures.label: Femoral bicondylar breadth (distal 60 mm, widest transverse extent, right)
measures.citation: no number read in an abstract
measures.note: internal reference = the two real donors measured by the same code (VH male, VH female); NOT a population norm (n = 1 + 1): VH male 91.4, VH female 81.7

measures.label: Biacromial breadth / bi-iliac breadth (skeletal, scapular acromion extremes)
measures.citation: no number read in an abstract
measures.note: biacromial 384.0 mm; internal reference = the two real donors measured by the same code (VH male, VH female); NOT a population norm (n = 1 + 1): VH male 1.37, VH female 1.106; arm position changes the scapulae

measures.label: Q angle (ASIS - patella centre - tibial tuberosity, coronal projection of the bone landmarks)
measures.note: the sex difference (2-3 deg) is far below the posture error of a supine cadaver with rotated legs (values 0.7 to 37 deg across the six pages): not measurable on these meshes

measures.label: Sternal length / width
measures.note: the Z-Anatomy 'sternum' is a different structure (119 / 108 / 95 mm vs 196 / 165 mm of the donors: manubrium + body vs the body piece): not comparable

measures.label: Breast: skin protrusion over the ribs at the breast level minus the sternal column
measures.note: supine cadaver, no gland modelled anywhere: the male donor reads 70 mm, the female donor 41 mm, the Z skin 49-64 mm: no sex signal; breast volume is NOT measurable

limits: Skeletal measurements use simple geometric landmark rules on decimated meshes of supine cadavers (not hand-placed osteometric landmarks): trust the sign of each difference, not the last digits.

Only the subpubic angle has a verified numeric reference (PMID 32274246); the other measures have a verified DIRECTION (PubMed abstracts) and are scored against the two real donors measured identically (n = 1 + 1, not a norm).

Skull dimorphism (mastoid, glabella, mental eminence, orbital margin) was NOT scored: the skull meshes exist (own pages: cranium, mandible, temporal, zygomatic; Z pages: frontal, occipital, maxilla, temporal, zygomatic, mandible) but automatic landmarking on 7,500-vertex decimated shells is not reliable; qualitative review of renders is left to the owner.

Obturator foramen shape was not measured (the foramen is a thin hole in a decimated shell; two attempts gave no stable outline). The pelvic inlet transverse / AP ratio was attempted by sectioning the P-SU plane and failed (the plane cuts the iliac blades, not the arcuate lines): reported as not measured instead of a wrong number.

Breast volume and gynoid / android fat could not be measured from the skin envelope (supine cadavers with arms on the trunk; the breasts added in Q234 are a sculpted reference model compressed into the skin envelope, not a measurement): the only fat-distribution evidence is the cryosection fat fractions of Q44 (below).
